title: Strata Insights activation — atelier sprint notes & runbook
content:
Context and objective:

This doc captures the sprint-level plan, workshop notes, checklist and the lightweight runbook for the Strata Insights pilot (3-week activation + 2-week validation). Goal: get a scoped Redwood Dedicated proof-of-value running on customer test data, with latency and cost baselines, two rollout candidates (quantized and full-precision), and a follow-up evaluation plan for quality/regression monitoring.

High-level success criteria (what we will hand off):
- End-to-end inference pipeline deployed in customer staging environment (VPC peering) with test dataset ingestion.
- Baseline throughput: 50 req/s sustained at p95 latency <= 220ms for short prompts (<=256 tokens).
- Cost estimate and recommended config: batching, KV cache policy, and quantization profile documented.
- Acceptance eval: pass 3/4 critical prompts (customer-defined) with >=95% acceptability as judged by SME.

Scope and non-goals:
- In-scope: model onboarding (open Llama variant), inference routing setup, SLO config, workspace access, canary rollout to 10% traffic, basic tracing integration to Redwood Console.
- Out-of-scope: full production data migration, custom model training, long-term retention policy (beyond 30d).

Sprint structure (week-by-week):
Week 0 (pre-kickoff, owner: Priya):
- Obtain customer network details and test dataset sample (3 payload types).
- Provision temporary Dedicated tenant and generate service account keys.
- Create shared Slack channel (redwood/strata-pilot).
- Questions for Strata: which 3 prompts are top priority? confirm latency SLO and peak concurrency windows.

Week 1 (kickoff + infra, owner: Alex):
- Day 0 workshop (2h): architecture walkthrough, mapping of services to customer VPC, responsibility matrix. Notes: customer prefers TLS mutual auth for ingress; security team to approve.
- Deliverable: infra diagram, CIDR allowances, KMS policy snapshot.
- Setup: Dedicated cluster with one g4dn-like pool (baseline), enable KV cache on runtime.
- Quick smoke test using synthetic inputs; collect p50/p95.

Week 2 (model tuning + routing, owner: Hannah):
- Add quantized variant (4-bit) and enable automatic fallback to fp16 when quality thresholds fail.
- Configure batching window heuristics and per-route batching size.
- Run 1k sample requests, capture latency, tokens/sec and failure rate.
- Observability: wire up per-route dashboard, add custom trace tags (customer_request_id, dataset_version).

Week 3 (canary + acceptance, owner: Marcus):
- Canary rollout: route 10% of test traffic to new deployment. Monitor for 48–72h.
- Execute acceptance eval set (customer prompts + edge cases). Compile pass/fail with notes.
- Cost modeling exercise: token rates, expected units per 1M requests for both variants.
- Handoff doc prepared: recommendations and next steps (Dedicated commit options).

Validation window (weeks 4–5):
- Customer-led trials and regression monitoring. Redwood to triage any quality drops and propose remediation (prompt engineering, model swap).

Day-of-workshop runbook (condensed checklist):
- Pre-meeting (24–48h): verify VPC peering, service account key valid, demo notebook loads sample data.
- Slide deck (10 slides): architecture, measurements so far, tests to run with attendees, success criteria.
- Roles during workshop: facilitator (Priya), infra lead (Alex), model tuning (Hannah), SRE escalation (Riley).
- Post-workshop: capture action items in linear backlog, assign owners, add follow-up meeting slot.

Acceptance tests (detailed):
- Perf acceptance: run 500 synthetic requests using customer average prompt; p95 <= 220ms for short prompts, error rate <0.5%.
- Functional acceptance: three named prompts must not hallucinate critical fields (fields A/B/C). SME signs off in doc.
- Operational acceptance: automatic rollback triggers functional on >1% error spikes or latency p95 > 400ms for 10m window.

Risk log (high priority entries):
- R1: Network policy lag from customer security delays VPC peering (mitigation: run a hosted sandbox for early perf testing; escalate via CSM).
- R2: Quantized model quality drop for long prompts (mitigation: configure fallback and keep fp16 variant as default for long sequences).
- R3: Autoscaler oscillations at low traffic volumes (mitigation: set min-replicas and stabilization window; SRE to tune HPA).
- R4: Cost uplift when burst traffic hits -- run token-rate cap and propose burst-tier pricing to customer.

Open questions / decisions needed (to capture in kickoff):
- What are the explicit data retention / logging controls Strata requires for PII? (security team input needed)
- Customer wants to test on a 10k-record dataset — confirm that sample is representative for latency conclusions.
- Final go/no-go criteria for committing to Dedicated 6-months.

Escalation contacts:
- Oncall SRE (primary): Riley Chen, slack @riley_sre, pager SRE-3
- Solutions lead: Priya Singhal, slack @priya_se, mobile +1-415-555-0119
- Customer success: Marcus Osei, slack @marcus-cs

Operational notes and quick commands (notes to self):
- If p95 spikes: check batching window and KV cache hit rate (console -> per-route cache metrics).
- To force rollback: post to /v1/rollouts with policy=rollback and tag=canary-20250214.
- Gather traces: set trace export to jaeger sandbox and attach trace id to JIRA ticket.

Metrics dashboard (tickets to create):
- Create Console dashboard: tokens/sec, p50/p95 latency, error rate, cache hit %, per-route cost estimate.
- Add a daily summary report to be emailed to Strata (owner: Marcus).

Notes from the kickoff (raw):
- Strata team: "we care about 95th percentile first — number-of-users less important than consistency".
- They will provide 3 canonical prompts and a holdout set for edge cases by 2025-02-14.
- Security asked for HSM-backed KMS; procurement needs a week. Potential blocker for Week1 infra.

Next actions (immediate):
- Priya: confirm workshop date with customer and get list of attendees (due 2025-02-12).
- Alex: start Dedicated tenant provisioning script and share terraform plan (due 2025-02-14).
- Hannah: prepare quantization checklist and the fallback policy draft (due 2025-02-16).
- Marcus: schedule daily 15m standups for weeks 1–3 and create Linear board.

Appendix: quick acceptance checklist (copyable)
- [ ] VPC peering established and tested
- [ ] Dedicated tenant ready with service account
- [ ] Baseline fp16 model deployed
- [ ] Quantized variant deployed + fallback policy configured
- [ ] Observability wired (dashboard + traces)
- [ ] Acceptance eval executed and results documented
- [ ] Cost model shared with customer
- [ ] Final recommendations and next steps doc ready

-- end of atelier sprint notes --

(Internal: keep a running log here as we complete tasks; we'll promote to final handoff doc after customer sign-off.)
